newsitem.title: USA: NATO ministers did not discuss new members.
newsitem.headline: NATO ministers did not discuss new members.

text.p: When NATO foreign ministers decided last week to invite the first former Soviet bloc countries to join the alliance in July they did not discuss even privately which ones, a NATO commander said on Tuesday.

"At the meetings last week there was no sense of who would be in the first tranch," British Vice Adm. Ian Garnett, deputy commander of NATO's Atlantic forces, said at a Pentagon briefing. "There was no explicit statement of who would be invited."
The NATO foreign ministers decided last Wednesday in Brussels to issue the first invitations at a NATO summit meeting in Madrid July 8 and 9.
There has been broad speculation that Poland, Hungary and the Czech and Slovakia republics might be among the first.

Garnett said those plus Romania and Moldavia were among nearly a dozen countries that have said they want to join NATO, with Romania listing that as a top foreign policy objective. But he said NATO must decide how many to invite in July while leaving the way open to invite more later.
The NATO official also said he believed NATO and new members would share costs of making their soldiers work with NATO allies.

"I am sure there will be a compromise, and clearly the countries joining NATO will contribute some resources and I imagine NATO too will contribute some. But we're some way from agreeing the details," he said.
